rich_summary: This section continues the story of Drona’s rise as the martial teacher of the Kuru princes. After being insulted and rejected by King Drupada, Drona arrives in Hastinapura and is honored by Bhishma, who entrusts all the Kuru princes—both Pandavas and Kauravas—to his instruction. Arjuna quickly distinguishes himself through intense discipline, cleverness, and devotion to his teacher, winning Drona’s special favor. The episode of Ekalavya reveals a darker side of the social order: though denied formal training because of his birth, Ekalavya teaches himself by worshipping a clay image of Drona and becomes a master archer, only to sacrifice his thumb as "tuition" when Drona demands it to preserve Arjuna’s supremacy. The chapter also establishes the specialties of each prince and ends with Drona preparing a famous test of skill—the bird’s-eye archery challenge.

highlight_spans.why: Drupada’s speech rejecting friendship across social ranks establishes the insult that motivates Drona’s later quest for revenge.
Drona’s wounded pride and vow after Drupada’s humiliation explain why he seeks pupils among the Kurus.
Arjuna’s vow to fulfill Drona’s hidden purpose marks the beginning of the deep bond between master and his greatest student.
Arjuna’s ingenuity in matching Aswatthaman’s advantage shows his relentless dedication and foreshadows his unmatched skill.
Ekalavya cutting off his thumb for Drona is one of the epic’s most emotionally powerful and morally debated moments.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ekalavya in the forest before a clay statue of Drona, practicing archery intensely while arrows blur through the air.
The dog returning to the Pandava princes with its mouth sealed by seven precisely placed arrows without a drop of blood.
Drona embracing Arjuna at night after hearing the twang of his bowstring as Arjuna secretly practices in the darkness.
